strongest_counterclaim: The 'dry-up' accumulation signal is a label-conditioned artifact. The two 'big_winner' cases are defined entirely by their outcome (W4 >= 8%), and their shared low-vol_ratio_5_20 trait is dominated by snapshot clustering and proxy contamination from is_b0_pick=false, not an independent coiled-spring mechanism. Adding a 0.9-1.2 vol_ratio_5_20 tier will introduce more entity_40ea0cfb3b-style ruins than it captures winners because low short-term volume is at least as diagnostic of neglect/illiquidity/falling-knife continuation as it is of accumulation.

attacks.issue: Severe selection-on-the-outcome in the false_negative label definition
attacks.why_it_matters: The 'false_negative_big_winner' class is constructed from stocks that (a) were rejected and (b) subsequently produced W4 >= 8%. Any 'pattern' observed within this class is a property of winners-once-rejected, not of rejected-stocks-in-general. Comparing medians of winners to medians of winners is circular; the only valid comparison is rejected-stocks-with-future-W4<8% vs. rejected-stocks-with-future-W4>=8%, which the method note does not show.

attacks.issue: Snapshot cluster confounder: >=4 of the 7 false-negatives and 2 of the 2 big-winner cases come from the single snapshot snap_71486ed83c
attacks.why_it_matters: When one snapshot contributes >50% of the cases in a class of 7, the within-class feature distribution reflects market conditions on that one date (a quiet tape, a sector rotation, a holiday-thin session) rather than stock-level accumulation. The 'dry-up profile' is partially a same-day artifact, not a repeatable per-stock signal. Reproducing it out-of-sample requires multiple snapshots, not just more cases.

attacks.issue: Proxy contamination: vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and pullback_pct are mechanically coupled through the recent price path
attacks.why_it_matters: A 20-day window that just produced only -5% pullback with mom_20 = +0.06 mechanically produces low realized volatility, low short-term volume bursts, and a middling up-day ratio. These three features are not three independent signals; they are one signal (recent realized variance) measured three ways. Splitting them and calling each a separate 'gate' overcounts evidence and inflates the apparent standardized deltas.

attacks.issue: Counter-examples from the same snapshot prove the dry-up tier is unsafe
attacks.why_it_matters: entity_40ea0cfb3b (snap_b8420124eb, vol_ratio_5_20=0.906, in the proposed 0.9-1.2 band, mom_20=0.024>0) is a B0-selected stock that RUINED. entity_ad2bfdee3f (snap_d0d57b1e40, vol_ratio_5_20=1.179, mom_20=-0.045) is a false-negative that produced only a small_win, not a large_win. These show the low-vol band is populated by both quiet accumulators and quiet deteriorations; the proposed up_day_ratio_20>=0.55 gate fails to separate them (entity_40ea0cfb3b has up_day_ratio_20=0.5, just below, but the proposed tier has no mechanism to keep it out at the next snapshot).

attacks.issue: Standardized deltas are computed on n=2 and n=7 with no confidence intervals; the headline numbers (-1.05, -1.19) are not statistically distinguishable from zero
attacks.why_it_matters: For n=7 the standard error of a median is approximately 1.25*IQR/sqrt(n). With IQRs around 0.2-0.4 on these scales, deltas of ~0.1-0.2 are within sampling noise. The claim 'standardized_delta = -1.19 is meaningful' requires bootstrap CIs the researcher did not provide; reporting only point estimates masquerades as evidence.

attacks.issue: The 'reduced pullback depth' of false-negatives is a mechanical consequence of weaker momentum, not a tight base
attacks.why_it_matters: false-negative median pullback_pct = -7.3% vs. selected_winner = -15.9%. The winners had DEEPER pullbacks (-25.1% for entity_2c58cebc59, -42.3% for entity_3adc078f01). A shallower pullback simply means the stock did not have a marked prior high to correct from. Calling this 'tighter base' reverses the IBD-style pattern where deep bases precede the strongest breakouts; it is post-hoc rationalization of the data.

attacks.issue: is_b0_pick=false carries information that is not captured by the auxiliary variables the researcher proposes adding back
attacks.why_it_matters: Stocks can be excluded from B0 for reasons beyond the few features in this dataset (sector exposure, earnings proximity, share-price liquidity, chart pattern type, news flow). The 'missed' signal could live in any of those unmeasured dimensions. Re-adding candidates via a 4-5 feature filter re-introduces all the original exclusions except the ones that happened to be captured by these proxies — a leaky sieve.

attacks.issue: The proposed mechanism ('supply absorption', 'coiled spring') is unfalsifiable within the snapshot
attacks.why_it_matters: Accumulation and quiet distribution are observationally identical at a snapshot. Without order-flow, dark-pool, or short-interest data, the same feature vector (low vol, positive mom, shallow pullback) can be narrated as either. A mechanism that explains any data is a mechanism that explains nothing; the empirical claim must stand on predictive lift, not on a story.

counterexamples_to_seek: All snap_71486ed83c cases removed: do the remaining false-negatives still cluster in the 0.9-1.2 vol_ratio_5_20 band? If the dry-up profile disappears when the dominant snapshot is dropped, the claim is a same-day artifact.

Stocks with vol_ratio_5_20 in [0.9, 1.2] and up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55 that DID NOT become big winners (failed dry-up candidates). Their frequency vs. the big-winner frequency in the same band is the only honest base-rate check. Specifically: how many such stocks ruined or had negative W4 in the discovery window?

Pairs matched on is_b0_pick=false, sector, and snapshot but differing in vol_ratio_5_20 (0.9 vs 1.6). If outcomes are uncorrelated with vol_ratio_5_20 within these pairs, vol_ratio_5_20 is not the signal.

Pre-period stability: do the same feature thresholds (vol_ratio_5_20 in [0.9,1.2], up_day_ratio_20 >= 0.55, mom_20 > 0) predict winners in the prior year? If not, the pattern is regime-specific and should not be deployed.

Look at entity_8ad5cd4795 specifically: a SELECTED winner (large_win) with vol_ratio_5_20=0.996 and ma20_slope_5=-0.0034. By the proposed dry-up logic this should have been a false-negative, but it was selected. Its presence in the winner column argues the existing filter is not systematically rejecting dry-up names — it accepted one already.
what_would_change_my_mind: An out-of-sample backtest on >=200 stocks outside the discovery window where the proposed dry-up tier achieves a large-win precision at least 1.5x the current B0-only baseline, with destroyed precision-on-ruin not statistically worse, and with the lift holding when snap_71486ed83c is excluded.

A within-snapshot matched analysis: conditioning on snapshot, sector, and is_b0_pick=false, the residual vol_ratio_5_20 band [0.9,1.2] predicts W4>=8% with odds ratio > 2 and p < 0.01 via logistic regression with appropriate multiple-testing correction.

Demonstration that the same feature set does NOT identify quiet-distribution names: i.e., vol_ratio_5_20 in [0.9,1.2] combined with negative mom_60 or negative ma50_slope_10 must NOT also predict wins, otherwise the 'signal' is just low-volatility drift in general.

Independent confirmation that the apparent standardized deltas on mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, and up_day_ratio_20 persist with non-overlapping bootstrap 95% CIs when recomputed on the same 7-vs-11 medians via permutation.

Any feature beyond those already in the table that the B0 filter uses and that, when added to the model, removes the marginal value of the proposed dry-up tier — i.e., showing the tier was reverse-engineered from winners rather than from the rejection logic.
